what: What one typo costs at the retrieval layer, and the decision not to fix it
why: Two of the sixteen questions a real install could not answer were misspelled - 'summaryze the second document', 'what is the list of priroities'. BM25 matches terms exactly, so a misspelled content word contributes nothing. Nobody had measured what that costs, and the plan said measure before building.
method: No model. For every golden case that names the document it must cite, the longest content word of the question - the most distinctive one, so the worst case for a single typo - is mangled four ways, and the question is asked again. The measure is whether the cited document is still among the six passages retrieved. A fact the model never sees is one it cannot state.
the_decision: Not built. 40 cases across four corpora, 160 question-and-typo pairs, and 156 still retrieve the document they need (97.5%) - one case in 40 is lost, and only in golden-ftr. A question carries several content words and BM25 finds the document on the others, so the single misspelling that motivated this is mostly absorbed already. A term-repair pass would be new machinery on the hot path of every query for 2.5% of one layer's recall.
not_measured: Whether a typo confuses the model even when retrieval succeeds. This is the retrieval ceiling only.
Two typos in one question, or a typo in a short content word rather than the longest.
Whether the embedding half of hybrid retrieval absorbs typos better than BM25; these runs are BM25-only.
a_mistake_worth_recording: The first version of this harness listed one directory level and only Markdown. evals/corpus/aveline is a tree with a spreadsheet and a PDF in it, so the harness measured an empty corpus and reported 0 of 14 found - a number that looked like a catastrophic finding and was a bug in the ruler. It now loads through the product's own parser, derives ids the way the connector does, and refuses to run on a corpus it cannot read or a case citing a document that is not there.
a_second_mistake: The sentence above was first written with numbers I had worked out in my head - 39 cases, 155 pairs - before the script printed 40 and 156. Nothing turned on the difference, which is exactly why it would have survived.
